records.title: Do short-term rental platforms affect housing markets? Evidence from Barcelona
records.design: Causal empirical analysis of short-term-rental platform expansion
records.finding: The study reports average rent +1.9%, transaction prices +4.6%, and posted prices +3.7% associated with platform activity.
limitations: Context-specific to Barcelona and its legal and housing market conditions.
Does not establish a universal effect size for all cities.

records.title: The effect of short-term rentals on house prices and residential mobility: evidence from Madrid
records.finding: The study reports that an increase of 100 entire-home listings raises house prices by about 2% and reduces residential inflows; it finds no significant effect on outflows.
limitations: The reported mobility mechanism is context-specific.
The result should not be transferred unchanged to every legal regime.

records.title: Does a 180-day cap on short-term rentals affect housing markets?
records.design: Dynamic causal analysis of a regulatory cap
records.finding: The study reports a temporary reduction in active short-term-rental listings and no sustained effect on long-term rents, consistent with weak enforcement or substitution.
limitations: A cap may behave differently with strong enforcement.
The result is not evidence that every form of regulation has no effect.

records.title: Drivers of Rent Arrears in Social Housing: an Evidence Review

source.publisher_or_journal: Sheffield Hallam University / Metropolitan Thames Valley Housing

records.finding: The review reports substantial arrears risk and identifies household financial circumstances and income shocks as central drivers.
limitations: UK-specific evidence.
The reported rates are not universal parameters for every housing system.

records.title: Right to Buy: Past, present and future
records.finding: The review records large-scale sales, substantial discounts, changing waiting lists, and questions about replacement of sold stock.
limitations: Policy effects interact with construction, benefits, migration, and local markets.
Administrative history is not a single causal estimate.

records.title: Madrid sale of public housing to vulture fund was illegal, report finds
records.design: Report of a regional audit finding irregularities
records.finding: The report describes lack of competition and transparency in the sale and subsequent tenant concerns.
limitations: A single administrative case cannot determine the effect of every disposal model.
The report focuses on irregularities and outcomes in this case.

records.title: Enabling Environments: Local Strategies for the Redevelopment of Public Land
records.finding: The article describes sale, lease, long-term ground lease, and deed restrictions as different tools with different trade-offs in control, revenue, and administrative burden.
limitations: Practice guidance is not a causal estimate.
Legal and institutional settings differ across cities.

records.title: Land Policy in Practice: A Tale of Two Dutch Cities

context.place: Dutch cities including Eindhoven and Amsterdam

records.finding: The account describes municipal land ownership, lease models, and the risk that land-lease income can create long-term fiscal or governance problems.
limitations: Not a controlled evaluation.
Interpretation depends on local institutional arrangements.

records.title: Impact of Rent Controls: Lessons from Catalonia
records.design: Economic analysis and review of policy effects
records.finding: The source reports lower rents in regulated markets alongside possible reductions in supply or composition effects, with interpretation depending on specification.
limitations: Results are sensitive to the comparison and outcome definition.
The policy and market changed over time.

records.title: The Perverse Effects of Rent Control: Evidence From a Large-scale Policy
records.finding: The source reports initially lower rents together with a substantial reduction in rental supply in the treated municipalities.
limitations: Interpretation differs from other analyses of the same policy.
Supply effects depend on legal details and enforcement.

records.title: Can zoning reform reduce housing costs? Evidence from rents in Auckland
records.finding: The source reports a 23% rent reduction relative to the synthetic control after the reform.
limitations: Auckland's reform, construction market, and geography are distinctive.
The result should not be treated as a universal effect size.

records.title: The local effects of relaxing land-use regulation on housing supply

source.publisher_or_journal: European Real Estate Society conference paper

records.finding: The source reports more housing supply but no significant rent change in the examined setting.
limitations: Conference-paper status and local context limit certainty.
Permits and completed units may differ.

records.title: Berlin expropriations would not ease housing shortage, study shows

source.publisher_or_journal: Reuters reporting on Kiel Institute analysis

records.finding: The reported analysis concludes that expropriation would not add enough stock to ease shortage and compares it with investment in new construction.
limitations: Projection rather than observed post-policy outcome.
Compensation, legal design, financing, and management assumptions drive the result.

records.title: How regulatory risk and expropriation threats are affecting Berlin's housing market
records.finding: The source reports changes in price-to-rent ratios and construction or investment responses associated with regulatory uncertainty.
limitations: The effect is about risk and expectations, not a direct estimate of expropriation itself.
Multiple policies and macroeconomic changes overlap.
